summary: 历史记录显示，欧洲人曾普遍分两段睡眠，中间有一段清醒时间。随着夜间生活和社会习惯改变，这种模式逐渐淡出；研究者借此讨论把连续八小时当成必然要求可能引起的焦虑。
logic: 质疑连续八小时的观念
史料里的第一觉和第二觉

paragraphs.brief: 分段睡眠属于自然现象的科学证据。
sentences: We often worry about lying awake in the middle of the night—but it could be good for you.
我们经常担心半夜睡醒... 但对你可能有好处
Indications from both science and history suggest that the eight-hour sleep may not be a natural or inborn pattern for humans.
科学和历史都表明，8小时的睡眠可能不是人类的自然或出生模式。
In the early 1990s, psychiatrist Thomas Wehr conducted research which implies just that.
1990年代初期，心理医生托马斯·韦尔进行了研究，这就意味着这一点。
Wehr kept a group of people in a darkened room for 14 hours a day for a month.
韦尔把一群人关在一个黑暗的房间里一天14小时一个月
It took some time for their sleep to regulate, but by the fourth week the subjects had settled into a very distinct sleeping pattern.
他们睡觉需要一些时间，但到了第四周，这些学员已经安顿下来，进入一种截然不同的睡眠模式。
First, they slept for four hours, then woke for one or two hours before falling into a second four-hour sleep.
首先，他们睡了四个小时，然后醒了一两个小时，然后又睡了四个钟头。
Though sleep scientists were impressed by the implications of the study, the idea that we must sleep for eight consecutive hours persists amongst the general public.
虽然睡眠科学家对研究的影响印象深刻，但公众仍然认为我们必须连续睡8个小时。

paragraphs.brief: 通过分析旧文献了解睡眠模式。
sentences: In 2001, historian Roger Ekirch of Virginia Tech University in the US published a paper drawn from 16 years of research, revealing historical evidence that humans used to sleep in two distinct periods of time each night.
2001年，美国弗吉尼亚技术大学历史学家Roger Ekirch发表了一篇论文，摘自16年的研究，其中揭示了人类过去每晚在两个不同时间睡觉的历史证据。
Ekirch’s research found more than 500 references to a segmented sleeping pattern—in diaries, court records, medical books and literature, from the ancient Greeks to tribes in Nigeria.
Ekirch的研究发现，从古希腊人到尼日利亚各部落，有500多处引用了片段睡眠模式——日记、法庭记录、医疗书籍和文献。
Much like Wehr’s findings, these references describe a first sleep which began not long following sunset.
与Wehr的发现很相似，这些引用描述了在日落后不久开始的第一次睡眠。
Then there was a waking period of one or two hours and after that a second sleep.
然后一两个小时的觉醒期之后又睡了第二个觉
During the waking period, people could be quite active.
在觉醒期间，人们可能相当活跃。
They sometimes got up and moved around the house, although most people stayed in bed, and perhaps read or wrote if they had enough money for candles.
他们有时站起来，四处走动，尽管大多数人都躺在床上，也许他们能读或写，如果他们有足够的钱来做蜡烛。
In many historic accounts, Ekirch found that people used the time that they were awake between periods of sleep to think about and attempt to analyse their dreams.
Ekirch在许多历史记录中发现，人们在睡觉期间用醒来的时间思考并试图分析自己的梦想。
In his book, Evening’s Empire, historian Craig Koslofsky suggests an explanation for this divided sleep pattern in Europe.
历史学家克雷格·科斯洛夫斯基在他的书《晚安帝国》中，为欧洲这种分裂的睡眠模式提出了一个解释。
‘Associations with night before the 17th century were not good,’ he writes.
他写道：「17世纪前的夜总会并不理想。
He goes on to explain that the streets of the cities and towns at night were often populated by thieves or worse.
他接着解释说，城市和城镇的街道在夜间往往有小偷或更坏的人。
The streets at night consequently scared many people.
晚上的街道让很多人害怕
Even the wealthy, who could afford to light their way, had better things to spend their nights on.
即使是有钱人，他们可以照亮他们的路，也有更好的东西，度过他们的夜晚。

paragraphs.brief: 分段睡眠为何逐渐少见的历史原因。
sentences: Ekirch found that references to the first and second sleep started to disappear during the late 17th century.
Ekirch发现，17世纪末，第一次和第二次睡眠的提法开始消失。
The pattern began to alter first among the upper classes in northern Europe and, over the course of the next 200 years, began changing amongst the rest of Western society.
这种模式开始在北欧的上层阶级中首先改变，在接下来的200年里，在西方社会的其他阶层中开始改变。
By the 1920s, the idea of a first and second sleep had receded entirely from our social consciousness.
到了20世纪20年代，第一次和第二次睡眠的想法已经完全从我们的社会意识中消失。
Ekirch attributes the initial shift to improvements in street and home lighting.
Ekirch将最初的转变归因于改善街道和住宅照明。
As the night became a time for all kinds of activity, the length of time people slept declined.
随着夜间成为各种活动的时间，人们睡觉的时间缩短了。
In 1667, Paris became the first city in the world to light its streets, using wax candles in glass lamps.
1667年，巴黎成为世界上第一个点燃街道的城市，使用玻璃灯中的蜡烛。
It was followed by another French city, Lille, in the same year and by Amsterdam in Holland two years later, where a much more efficient oil-powered lamp was developed.
紧随其后的是同年另一个法国城市里尔，两年后阿姆斯特丹在荷兰开发了一个效率更高的石油动力灯。
London didn’t light its streets until 1684, but by the end of the 17th century, more than 50 of Europe’s major towns and cities were lit at night.
伦敦直到1684年才点燃街道但到了17世纪末超过50个欧洲主要城镇和城市的灯光在夜间点燃
Coffee houses emerged as a fashionable phenomenon and many were open virtually around the clock.
咖啡馆成为一种时髦的现象，许多咖啡馆几乎全天营业。
Going out at night became commonplace, and spending hours lying in bed was considered a waste of time.
晚上出门变得司空见惯，躺在床上的时间被认为是浪费时间。
‘People were becoming increasingly time-conscious and sensitive to efficiency, certainly before the 19th century,’ says Ekirch.
在19世纪之前，艾基奇也这么说：“人们越来越有时间性，对效率越来越敏感。”
‘But the Industrial Revolution intensified that attitude considerably.’
但工业革命大大强化了这种态度。
Strong evidence of this shifting attitude is contained in a medical journal from 1829 which urged parents to force their children out of the pattern of first and second sleep.
1829年的医学期刊中载有这种转变态度的有力证据，其中敦促父母强迫其子女离开第一次和第二次睡眠模式。

paragraphs.brief: 使人醒后难以再入睡的生物及环境因素。
sentences: Today, most people seem to have adapted quite well to the eight-hour sleep, but Ekirch believes many sleeping problems may have roots in the human body’s natural preference for divided sleep, as well as in difficulties caused by extended exposure to artificial light in the modern world.
今天，大多数人似乎适应了8小时的睡眠，但Ekirch认为，许多睡眠问题的根源可能在于人体自然偏爱分裂睡眠，以及现代世界人造光照射的扩大所造成的困难。
This could be the cause of a condition called sleep maintenance insomnia, where people wake during the night and have trouble getting back to sleep.
这可能是造成失眠症的原因，人晚上醒来后很难回去睡觉。
The condition first appears in literature at the end of the 19th century, at the same time as accounts of interrupted sleep disappear.
19世纪末，文学界首次出现这种情况，同时，关于睡眠中断的叙述也消失了。

paragraphs.brief: 可能与睡眠有关的健康问题。
sentences: Sleep psychologist Gregg Jacobs says that the idea that we must sleep for an extended period of time could be damaging if it makes people who wake up in the night anxious, as this anxiety can itself discourage sleep and is likely to affect waking life too.
睡眠心理学家Gregg Jacobs说，如果让人们在夜间醒来时感到焦虑，那么，我们必须长时间睡觉的想法可能会造成损害，因为这种焦虑本身会妨碍睡眠，而且会影响到醒来的生活。
Jacobs suggests that the waking period between sleeps, when people simply rested and relaxed, could have played an important part in the human capacity to regulate stress naturally.
Jacobs认为，人们睡不着觉的时期，即人们只是休息和放松的时候，在人自然调节压力的能力方面可以发挥重要作用。
Russell Foster, a professor of circadian (body clock) neuroscience at Oxford University in the UK, shares this point of view.
罗素福斯特，英国牛津大学生理钟神经科学教授赞同这一观点
‘Over 30% of the medical problems that doctors are faced with stem directly or indirectly from sleep.
超过30%的医生面临直接或间接因睡眠而缺血的医疗问题。
But sleep has been ignored in medical training, and there are very few centres where sleep is studied,’ Foster says.
Foster说，很少有中心可以学习睡眠：“但是在医疗训练中，睡眠被忽略了。”
He feels this needs to change.
他觉得这需要改变

长时间处于黑暗的受试者自然睡成两段，历史文献里反复出现的第一觉与第二觉也呈现相似安排。
解释夜晚的作息为何改变
街灯、咖啡馆和夜生活改变了人们使用夜晚的方式，效率观念的兴起也令分段睡眠渐渐少见。
重新理解半夜醒来的经验
当一觉到天亮成为常规，夜间醒来本身可能引发忧虑，结尾据此讨论睡眠困扰和医学训练该关注什么。

items.en: In certain historical periods, the threat of criminal danger led to segmented sleep.
items.zh: 在某些历史时期，犯罪危险的威胁导致睡眠分裂。

items.en: Physicians should learn more about treating people with sleeping difficulties.
items.zh: 医生应该更多地了解如何治疗有睡眠困难的人。

items.en: Historically, when people experienced interrupted sleep, they used the waking periods at night for different activities.
items.zh: 从历史上看，当人们经历中断的睡眠时，他们利用夜间的觉醒时间进行不同的活动。

items.en: Technological changes in Europe made people more likely to sleep through the night.
items.zh: 欧洲的技术变革使人们更有可能在夜间睡觉。

items.en: The belief that humans should have a long continuous sleep can be psychologically harmful.
items.zh: 认为人类应长期连续睡觉，这种信念在心理上是有害的。

items.en: People habitually went to bed early, soon after ________, slept for a while, then woke up for a few hours of activity or perhaps to consider, for example, the meaning of their ____ (Q25).
items.zh: 过去人们习惯早睡，往往在________后不久就上床。睡过一阵再醒来，活动几个小时，也可能思索自己的________（Q25）有什么含义。
items.why: 空格需要“在…之后不久”的时间点。原文对应 Sunset。

items.en: People habitually went to bed early, soon after ____ (Q24), slept for a while, then woke up for a few hours of activity or perhaps to consider, for example, the meaning of their ________.
items.zh: 过去人们习惯早睡，往往在________（Q24）后不久就上床。睡过一阵再醒来，活动几个小时，也可能思索自己的________有什么含义。

items.en: In 16th-century Europe, people tended to stay at home at night because they feared ________ on largely unlit city streets.
items.zh: 16 世纪的欧洲人晚上通常待在家中，因为城市街道几乎没有照明，他们担心遇上________。
items.why: 空格需表示让人害怕的对象。原文为 thieves。

clauses: Indications from both science and history suggest ….
“that the eight-hour sleep may not be a natural or inborn pattern for humans”补足 suggest 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 suggest 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, the idea that we must sleep for eight consecutive hours persists amongst the general public.
连接词 though 引出“Though sleep scientists were impressed by the implications of the study”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 though 把这一层关系补进去。
